JOINT DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT

This Joint Development Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into on the 15th day of March, 2022 at Gurugram, Haryana.

BETWEEN:
Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at 4th Floor, Tower B, DLF Cyber City, Gurugram, Haryana 122002 (hereinafter referred to as the "Landowner/First Party")

AND:
Apex Constructions Ltd., a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at 12, Udyog Vihar, Phase IV, Gurugram, Haryana 122015 (hereinafter referred to as the "Developer/Second Party")

WHEREAS the First Party is the owner of land admeasuring 5.2 acres situated at Sector 72, Gurugram, Haryana, bearing Khasra No. 142/3, 143/1, and 144/2 (hereinafter referred to as the "Said Property");

AND WHEREAS the parties have agreed to jointly develop the Said Property into a residential housing project comprising approximately 320 residential units across 4 towers (hereinafter referred to as the "Project");

NOW THIS AGREEMENT WITNESSETH AS FOLLOWS:

CLAUSE 4 — PROJECT TIMELINE AND MILESTONES

4.1 The Developer shall commence construction within 90 days of obtaining all necessary approvals and sanctions from the competent authorities including DTCP and HRERA.

4.2 The Developer shall complete the entire Project, including all four towers, common areas, and amenities, within 24 months from the date of commencement of construction, i.e., by 31st March, 2024 (hereinafter the "Completion Date").

4.3 The Completion Date may be extended only upon mutual written consent of both parties, and any extension shall not exceed 6 months without invoking the penalty provisions under Clause 9.

CLAUSE 5 — FINANCIAL TERMS AND REVENUE SHARING

5.1 The total estimated project cost is Rs. 85,00,00,000/- (Rupees Eighty-Five Crores Only).

5.2 The Landowner shall contribute the land valued at Rs. 32,00,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Two Crores Only) as determined by the registered valuer's report dated 10th February 2022.

5.3 The Developer shall invest Rs. 53,00,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty-Three Crores Only) towards construction costs, regulatory approvals, and project management.

5.4 Revenue sharing shall be in the ratio of 38:62 (Landowner:Developer) from the gross sale proceeds of all residential and commercial units.

5.5 The Landowner has advanced Rs. 12,50,00,000/- (Rupees Twelve Crores Fifty Lakhs Only) to the Developer as mobilisation advance, to be adjusted against the Developer's share of revenue.

CLAUSE 7 — QUALITY STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS

7.1 The Developer shall use construction materials conforming to IS standards as specified in Annexure C attached hereto.

7.2 All structural steel shall be of Fe-500D grade or equivalent as per IS 1786:2008.

7.3 Concrete grade shall not be below M-30 for foundations and M-25 for superstructure as certified by the appointed structural engineer.

7.4 The Developer shall engage an independent third-party quality auditor approved by the Landowner to conduct quarterly inspections.

CLAUSE 9 — PENALTY AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS

9.1 In the event the Developer fails to achieve the completion milestone by the Completion Date, a penalty of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) per week of delay shall be levied, subject to a maximum of Rs. 2,00,00,000/- (Rupees Two Crores Only).

9.2 If the delay exceeds 6 months beyond the Completion Date, the Landowner shall have the right to terminate this Agreement and seek damages including but not limited to the mobilisation advance, opportunity cost, and consequential losses.

9.3 The Developer shall not assign, transfer, or delegate any rights or obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the prior written consent of the Landowner.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have executed this Agreement on the date first above written.

For Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd.
Sd/- Mr. Rajesh Kapoor, Managing Director

For Apex Constructions Ltd.
Sd/- Mr. Vikram Malhotra, Chairman & Managing Director

SUPPLEMENTARY AGREEMENT / ADDENDUM

Date: 18th October, 2023

This Supplementary Agreement ("Addendum") is entered into between Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd. ("First Party") and Apex Constructions Ltd. ("Second Party") in relation to the Joint Development Agreement dated 15th March, 2022.

WHEREAS both parties acknowledge that the Project has experienced delays attributable to regulatory approvals from HRERA and unexpected soil conditions at the site;

WHEREAS the Developer has represented that the Project is 62% complete as of the date of this Addendum;

NOW THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows:

1. REVISED COMPLETION DATE: The Completion Date under Clause 4.2 of the Original Agreement is hereby extended to 30th June, 2024.

2. ADDITIONAL INVESTMENT: The Developer shall infuse an additional Rs. 8,00,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Crores Only) within 45 days of execution of this Addendum to accelerate construction.

3. PENALTY WAIVER: Penalties accrued under Clause 9.1 up to the date of this Addendum, amounting to Rs. 65,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Five Lakhs Only), are hereby waived by the Landowner as a gesture of goodwill.

4. QUALITY AUDIT: The Developer shall, within 30 days of this Addendum, engage M/s Larsen & Toubro Technical Services or equivalent Grade-A auditor to conduct a comprehensive structural audit and submit the report to the Landowner.

5. ESCROW ARRANGEMENT: All future sale proceeds from pre-booked units shall be deposited into a joint escrow account at HDFC Bank, Gurugram Branch, to ensure transparency of fund utilisation.

6. NO FURTHER EXTENSIONS: Both parties agree that no further extensions beyond 30th June, 2024 shall be granted. Failure to complete by this revised date shall automatically trigger the termination provisions under Clause 9.2 of the Original Agreement.

7. All other terms and conditions of the Original Agreement dated 15th March, 2022 shall remain unchanged and in full force.

For Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd.
Sd/- Mr. Rajesh Kapoor, Managing Director
Date: 18.10.2023

For Apex Constructions Ltd.
Sd/- Mr. Vikram Malhotra, Chairman & Managing Director
Date: 18.10.2023

Witness 1: Sd/- Adv. Neha Sharma (Advocate, Delhi High Court)
Witness 2: Sd/- CA Suresh Agarwal (Chartered Accountant)

SITE INSPECTION REPORT
Prepared by: Er. Anand Krishnan, B.Tech, M.Tech (Structural), FIE
Consulting Structural Engineer — Engaged by Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd.

Inspection Date: 15th January, 2024
Project: Residential Development, Sector 72, Gurugram
Weather: Clear, 14°C

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
Upon thorough physical inspection of the project site spanning two full working days, the undersigned observes that the overall construction progress stands at approximately 45% completion as against the scheduled 90% that should have been achieved by this date per the original project timeline.

TOWER-WISE ASSESSMENT:
- Tower A: Structural work completed up to 12th floor (of 18 planned floors). Significant honeycombing observed in concrete at floors 8 and 9. Rebar spacing non-compliant with IS 456:2000 at multiple locations.
- Tower B: Structural work completed up to 8th floor. Work appears to have been suspended for approximately 3 weeks based on concrete curing condition.
- Tower C: Foundation and basement complete. Ground floor columns erected. No further progress.
- Tower D: Only excavation and piling completed. No superstructure work commenced.

QUALITY OBSERVATIONS:

1. CONCRETE QUALITY: Core samples extracted from Tower A, Floor 8, indicate concrete compressive strength of M-20 to M-22 grade, which is significantly below the M-30 minimum specified in Clause 7.3 of the JDA for foundations and M-25 for superstructure. This constitutes a material breach of the agreed quality specifications.

2. STEEL QUALITY: Mill test certificates reviewed for steel used in Tower B indicate Fe-415 grade steel in several consignments, contrary to the Fe-500D requirement under Clause 7.2 of the JDA. Approximately 340 MT of non-compliant steel appears to have been used.

3. WATERPROOFING: Basement waterproofing in Towers A and B shows visible seepage at multiple locations. The waterproofing membrane appears to be of inferior quality and improperly applied.

4. SAFETY CONCERNS: Multiple safety violations observed including absence of fall protection systems, inadequate scaffolding, and exposed electrical wiring.

CONCLUSION: The project is severely behind schedule and exhibits multiple instances of substandard construction that compromise structural integrity. Immediate remedial measures are essential. The current construction quality raises serious concerns about the long-term safety and durability of the structures.

Sd/- Er. Anand Krishnan
Date: 20th January, 2024
Registration No.: CE/HR/2015/4432

PROGRESS ASSESSMENT REPORT
Prepared by: M/s Skyline Engineering Consultants Pvt. Ltd.
Commissioned by: Apex Constructions Ltd.

Assessment Date: 22nd January, 2024
Project: Premium Residences, Sector 72, Gurugram

PROJECT STATUS OVERVIEW:
Based on our comprehensive assessment conducted over three working days, the overall project completion stands at 78% which represents substantial progress considering the regulatory delays and force majeure conditions encountered during the monsoon season.

TOWER-WISE PROGRESS:
- Tower A: 95% structural completion. All 18 floors completed. Internal finishing and MEP work in progress on floors 1-12. Minor cosmetic issues noted, all within acceptable IS code tolerances.
- Tower B: 80% structural completion. Structure complete up to 15th floor. Internal works commenced on lower floors.
- Tower C: 55% complete. Structure up to 6th floor. Progressing as per revised schedule.
- Tower D: 40% complete. Foundation, basement, and ground floor structure complete. Vertical construction actively in progress.

QUALITY ASSESSMENT: All construction materials tested are within acceptable parameters. Concrete cube test results from our laboratory confirm M-25 to M-30 grade compliance across all towers.

MATERIAL COMPLIANCE:

1. CONCRETE: Cube test results from our NABL-accredited laboratory (Report Nos. CT/2024/0145 to CT/2024/0168) confirm compressive strength ranging from 28.5 MPa to 34.2 MPa, meeting the M-25/M-30 specifications.

2. STEEL: All steel procured from TATA Steel and JSW Steel, accompanied by valid mill test certificates confirming Fe-500D grade compliance. Total steel consumed to date: 2,840 MT.

3. WATERPROOFING: Integral crystalline waterproofing system applied as per manufacturer specifications. Minor condensation marks observed in basement are seasonal and not indicative of structural waterproofing failure.

TIMELINE ASSESSMENT:
The project has experienced a cumulative delay of approximately 4.5 months attributable to:
- HRERA registration delays: 2 months
- Unprecedented rainfall (July-September 2023): 1.5 months
- Labour shortage during festival season: 1 month

These are force majeure events beyond the Developer's control. With the current pace, the revised completion date of August 2024 is achievable.

RECOMMENDATION: The project is proceeding satisfactorily. The Developer's team is competent and the quality of construction meets all applicable Indian standards.

Sd/- Er. Prashant Gupta, Director
M/s Skyline Engineering Consultants Pvt. Ltd.
Date: 28th January, 2024

DISCREPANCY NOTE:

2. No utilisation certificates have been provided by Apex Constructions for any of the payments made after the mobilisation advance, despite repeated written requests dated 15-Sep-2023 and 01-Nov-2023.

3. Site verification by our accounts team on 12-Dec-2023 revealed that material procurement invoices submitted by Apex total only Rs. 14,50,00,000/- against the Rs. 20,25,00,000/- received, leaving Rs. 5,75,00,000/- unaccounted for.

This discrepancy note was shared with Apex Constructions vide email dated 05-Jan-2024. No response has been received as of the preparation of this statement.

Under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

Date: 25th February, 2024

Mr. Vikram Malhotra, Chairman & Managing Director
Apex Constructions Ltd.
12, Udyog Vihar, Phase IV, Gurugram, Haryana 122015

(On behalf of Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd.)

Sub: Legal Notice for breach of Joint Development Agreement dated 15.03.2022 and Supplementary Agreement dated 18.10.2023 — Demand for Rs. 52,25,00,000/- and termination of Agreement.

Sir,

Under instructions from our client, Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd., we hereby serve upon you this Legal Notice:

1. That our client entered into a JDA with your company on 15.03.2022 for development of residential project at Sector 72, Gurugram.

2. That despite receiving total payments of Rs. 20,25,00,000/- and having use of land valued at Rs. 32,00,00,000/-, your company has failed to complete the project. As per our client's engineer's report dated 20.01.2024, the project is merely 45% complete — far short of the 100% completion required by 30.06.2024.

REPLY TO LEGAL NOTICE

Date: 20th March, 2024

To:
Advocate Priya Mehta
M/s Mehta & Associates
305, Lawyers' Chambers, Delhi High Court, New Delhi 110003

From:
Advocate Sunil Khanna (Enrolment No. D/8912/2010)
M/s Khanna & Partners, Advocates & Solicitors
15th Floor, One Horizon Centre, Golf Course Road, Gurugram 122002
(On behalf of Apex Constructions Ltd.)

Madam,

We are in receipt of your Legal Notice dated 25.02.2024 and deny all allegations contained therein. The facts are as follows:

1. Our client has at all times acted in good faith and in compliance with the JDA.

2. The project is 78% complete as confirmed by our independent engineer's assessment dated 28.01.2024. Your client's engineer's report is biased, outdated, and based on a cursory one-day inspection.

3. Our client has received only Rs. 8,30,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Crores Thirty Lakhs Only) from Meridian Realty against the claimed Rs. 20,25,00,000/-. The balance amount of Rs. 4,20,00,000/- from the mobilisation advance was never disbursed despite repeated requests. Your client's payment schedule is fabricated and we demand production of original bank statements.

4. The allegation regarding substandard materials is categorically denied. All construction materials are IS-compliant as evidenced by our NABL-accredited laboratory reports. The alleged M-20 grade concrete finding is scientifically impossible given that our concrete is batched at our own RMC plant with automated quality controls.

5. The delay in the project is entirely attributable to force majeure events and non-cooperation by your client, including:
   (a) Failure to obtain timely environmental clearance — 3 months delay
   (b) Unprecedented monsoon rainfall in 2023 — 1.5 months
   (c) Delayed payment of mobilisation advance tranches — 2 months
   (d) Your client's refusal to approve design modifications necessitated by soil conditions — 1 month

6. The payment to PNB account was for material procurement from a vendor. The account belongs to M/s VM Enterprises, a legitimate material supplier, not a personal account.

7. The Addendum dated 18.10.2023 was signed under economic duress and is voidable under Section 19A of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

Our client reserves all rights to file a counter-claim for damages caused by your client's non-cooperation and defamatory allegations.

Sd/- Advocate Sunil Khanna
M/s Khanna & Partners

APEX CONSTRUCTIONS LTD.
MINUTES OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING

Date: 14th September, 2023
Time: 11:00 AM
Venue: Conference Room, 12 Udyog Vihar, Phase IV, Gurugram

Present:
1. Mr. Vikram Malhotra — Chairman & Managing Director
2. Ms. Sunita Malhotra — Director
3. Mr. Deepak Sharma — Independent Director
4. Mr. Rajeev Gupta — CFO

Item 3: Status of Sector 72 Project (Meridian JDA)

The CMD briefed the Board on the current status:
- Construction progress: approximately 52% complete
- Fund utilisation: Rs. 18,40,00,000/- spent against Rs. 20,25,00,000/- received
- Remaining budget shortfall: approximately Rs. 28,00,00,000/- to complete

The CMD informed the Board that the company faces a severe cash flow crisis due to:
(a) Unsold inventory in two other projects (Sector 58 and Sector 89)
(b) Outstanding payments from homebuyers totalling Rs. 34,00,00,000/-
(c) Bank loan EMI obligations of Rs. 1,80,00,000/- per month

The CMD proposed diverting Rs. 3,50,00,000/- from the Sector 72 project escrow to meet urgent EMI obligations for the Sector 89 project, to avoid the Sector 89 loan being classified as NPA.

DISCUSSION ON FUND DIVERSION:

Mr. Deepak Sharma (Independent Director) raised objections to the proposed fund diversion, stating that it would constitute a breach of fiduciary duty and violate the terms of the JDA with Meridian Realty. He noted that the JDA explicitly prohibits use of project funds for any purpose other than the Sector 72 development.

The CMD responded that the diversion would be temporary (30-45 days) and would be replenished from expected receivables from the Sector 58 project.

Resolution: The Board approved the temporary diversion of Rs. 3,50,00,000/- by a vote of 3:1, with Mr. Deepak Sharma recording his dissent. The CFO was directed to ensure the amount is returned to the Sector 72 project account within 45 days.

Item 4: Material Procurement Cost Optimisation

The CFO presented a proposal to switch from Fe-500D steel (current rate: Rs. 62,000/MT) to Fe-415 grade steel (rate: Rs. 51,000/MT) for non-structural elements to save approximately Rs. 1,50,00,000/- on the remaining steel requirement.

The CMD approved the proposal noting that Fe-415 is adequate for non-critical structural members and the cost savings are essential given the budget shortfall.

Mr. Deepak Sharma again dissented, noting that the JDA specifies Fe-500D grade for all structural steel without distinction between critical and non-critical members.

Meeting concluded at 1:45 PM.

Sd/- Company Secretary
Ms. Priti Chhabra

Dear Mr. Gupta,

During our year-end reconciliation, we have identified that against total disbursements of Rs. 20,25,00,000/- to Apex Constructions, the material procurement invoices and documented expenditure total only Rs. 14,50,00,000/-. This leaves Rs. 5,75,00,000/- unaccounted.

Furthermore, we have identified that RTGS payment of Rs. 2,80,00,000/- (UTR: HDFC23042000698) was credited to PNB A/c No. 6145002100098765 instead of the designated SBI project account. Our records indicate this PNB account is not in the name of Apex Constructions Ltd.

Please provide:
1. Complete utilisation certificates for all amounts received
2. Clarification on the PNB account and its beneficiary
3. Audited project expenditure statement

We require your response within 7 working days.

Regards,
Kavita Nair, CFO
Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd.

--- Email 4 ---
From: rajeev.gupta@apexconstructions.in
To: kavita.nair@meridianrealty.in
Date: 22 January 2024, 6:15 PM
Subject: Re: URGENT — Fund Reconciliation Discrepancy of Rs. 5.75 Crore

Dear Ms. Nair,

We are compiling the requested documents and will revert shortly. The PNB account belongs to M/s VM Enterprises, our authorised material supplier for steel and cement. Payments were routed through this account for operational efficiency.

Regards,
Rajeev Gupta, CFO
Apex Constructions Ltd.

--- Email 5 ---
From: rajesh.kapoor@meridianrealty.in
To: vikram.malhotra@apexconstructions.in
Date: 10 February 2024, 9:00 AM
Subject: Final Warning — Non-compliance with Addendum and Fund Misappropriation

Dear Mr. Malhotra,

This is a final written communication before we proceed to legal action.

As of today:
1. The Rs. 8 Crore additional investment promised in the Addendum has NOT been made (4 months overdue)
2. No Grade-A structural audit has been conducted (3 months overdue)
3. No escrow account has been opened
4. The Rs. 5.75 Crore discrepancy remains unexplained — your CFO's response of 22 January was evasive
5. M/s VM Enterprises (PNB A/c beneficiary) shares its registered address with your personal residence at 45, Sushant Lok, Phase I, Gurugram — this raises serious concerns about fund diversion

We have also received information that your company has been diverting funds from our project to service loan obligations for your Sector 89 project. If true, this constitutes criminal breach of trust under Section 405 of the Indian Penal Code.

We are left with no option but to engage legal counsel and initiate civil and criminal proceedings.

Rajesh Kapoor
MD, Meridian Realty Group

INDEPENDENT VALUATION REPORT

Prepared by: M/s Cushman & Wakefield India Pvt. Ltd.
Date: 28th February, 2024
Commissioned by: Meridian Realty Group Pvt. Ltd.

PROPERTY: Land and ongoing construction at Sector 72, Gurugram (Meridian Heights Project)

1. LAND VALUATION:
   - Current market value of 5.2 acres in Sector 72: Rs. 48,00,00,000/- (Rupees Forty-Eight Crores Only)
   - Appreciation since JDA execution (March 2022): 50% (valued at Rs. 32 Cr in JDA)
   - Per-acre value: Rs. 9.23 Crores (current) vs Rs. 6.15 Crores (at JDA)

2. CONSTRUCTION VALUE:
   - Estimated value of construction completed (at 45% completion): Rs. 22,50,00,000/-
   - Cost to complete remaining 55%: Rs. 34,00,00,000/- (estimated)
   - Remediation cost for substandard construction (Towers A & B): Rs. 4,50,00,000/- (estimated)

3. PROJECT VIABILITY ASSESSMENT:
   - Estimated total sellable area: 4,80,000 sq. ft.
   - Current prevailing rate in Sector 72: Rs. 8,500-9,500 per sq. ft.
   - Estimated gross revenue upon completion: Rs. 432,00,00,000/- to Rs. 456,00,00,000/-
   - The project remains commercially viable despite the delays, provided construction quality issues are remediated.

4. LOSS ASSESSMENT:

   (a) Loss due to construction delay (opportunity cost at 12% per annum on Rs. 52.25 Cr for 18 months): Rs. 9,40,50,000/-

   (b) Diminution in project value due to market perception of delayed project: Estimated 8-12% discount on sellable rates, translating to approximately Rs. 38,00,00,000/- in reduced revenue.

   (c) Cost of remediation for substandard materials: Rs. 4,50,00,000/-

   (d) Additional regulatory compliance costs (HRERA penalties, revised registrations): Rs. 75,00,000/-

   TOTAL ESTIMATED LOSS TO LANDOWNER: Rs. 52,65,50,000/- (Rupees Fifty-Two Crores Sixty-Five Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only)

5. CONCLUSION:

Based on our independent assessment, the Landowner (Meridian Realty Group) has suffered substantial financial loss due to:
- Construction delays beyond contracted timelines
- Use of substandard materials necessitating remediation
- Apparent fund diversion reducing project investment
- Market perception damage to the project brand
